newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lawyers say German charges filed against tycoon.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers say German charges filed against tycoon.

text.p: Lawyers for Juergen Schneider, blamed for one of the most spectacular corporate collapses in German history, said Sunday that prosecutors had filed criminal charges against the disgraced tycoon.
Schneider's lawyer, Christoph Rueckel, did not detail the charges against Schneider. He previously has said they would include fraud, falsifying documents and fraudulent bankruptcy.

Frankfurt prosecutors will hold a news conference Monday to announce details of the charges against Schneider, whose real estate empire collapsed in April 1994 under the weight of some five billion marks ($3.2 billion) in debt.
A trial is not expected to start before mid-1997.

Rueckel said the Schneider, 62, who was once one of Germany's most celebrated entrepreneurs, was committed to fighting the allegations and reiterated that German banks that lent money to Schneider were also responsible for his collapse.

The charges are expected to allege that Schneider received credit on the basis of falsified documents, such as overstating expected rental income. He then slid into bankruptcy as the rental income was too low to service the mounting debt.
Schneider and his wife, Claudia, were detained in Miami in 1995 following a year-long international manhunt. They returned voluntarily to Germany last February to face questioning.
Schneider, who ran his empire from a castle-like villa in the Taunus Hills near Frankfurt, has been detained in a Frankfurt area prison since his return to Germany.
Claudia Schneider, who is expected to be charged with being an accessory to bankruptcy, has been freed from prison on conditional release amid concerns about her health.
